Change c0483. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): Sometimes, when nature, overcome by hunger, sunk under the exhaustion, a repast was prepared for me in the desert, that restored and inspirited me.

1818 text: The fare was indeed coarse, such as the peasants of the country ate; but I may not doubt that it was set there by the spirits that I had invoked to aid me.

1831 text: The fare was, indeed, coarse, such as the peasants of the country ate; but I will not doubt that it was set there by the spirits that I had invoked to aid me.

Diff: The fare was {+,+} indeed {+,+} coarse, such as the peasants of the country ate; but I [-may-] {+will+} not doubt that it was set there by the spirits that I had invoked to aid me.

Context after (unchanged): Often, when all was dry, the heavens cloudless, and I was parched by thirst, a slight cloud would bedim the sky, shed the few drops that revived me, and vanish.

result.rationale: "may not doubt" becomes "will not doubt", making the Creature's belief in the spirits' provision more assertive and less hedged; the added commas are punctuation only. The supernatural attribution stays but is firmer.
